tree_details.subject: Pair-interaction arithmetic and reciprocal-square-root optimization
tree_details.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, investigate reducing pair-interaction math while retaining one thread per output. Try direct rsqrtf(distSq) with explicit reciprocal-cube multiplies and, if correct, algebraic cancellation of the target mass in the acceleration coefficient. Keep self-interaction skipping, float32 softening and update semantics, exact mass copying, and the existing single-kernel ABI. Do not enable global fast math or add launches or buffers. Validate every required case and compare the three-repeat benchmark geometric mean; provide the best correct source and launch.json.

tree_details.subject: Warp-cooperative source summation per output
tree_details.objective: Investigate assigning one warp to each output particle: lanes accumulate partial forces over distinct source indices and reduce the three components within the warp. Keep the pair arithmetic close to the supplied implementation to isolate this mapping change. Correctly handle tails, self-interaction, complete output state, and arbitrary supported N; tune block and items_per_block consistently. Validate the changed summation order against all required tolerances, then measure the official geometric mean and report the best correct source and launch.json.

tree_details.subject: CTA shared-memory source tiling
tree_details.objective: Investigate staging source Particle records in CTA shared memory, with one thread owning each output and reusing each staged source across the CTA's outputs. Handle source and output tails, synchronization, and the allowed shared-memory limit; tune the tile and launch configuration without adding a kernel or allocation. Keep the supplied force arithmetic/order as far as practical to isolate the reuse strategy. Validate all required cases and compare the official geometric mean; provide the best correct source and launch.json.

tree_details.subject: Explore staging source positions and mass in shared memory in source chunks so multiple target threads reuse each staged source. Keep the output mapping at one target per thread to distinguish this from register-blocked output work. Tune a valid block/items_per_block/shared_memory_bytes configuration and the shared tile layout; handle partial source and target tiles without letting inactive threads skip required barriers. Preserve i==j exclusion, the exact interface and all correctness requirements. Compare using the prescribed three-size geometric-mean kernel-time objective, and retain only candidates that pass the full correctness checks.
tree_details.objective: Shared-memory source tiling, one target per thread

tree_details.subject: Explore assigning a small batch of target particles to each thread, with separate accumulators, so a source particle's loaded position and mass can be reused across those targets. This is an output-axis/register-reuse investigation, not merely another one-target-per-thread shared-memory tile. Tune the batch size and allowed launch configuration while monitoring register pressure and available parallelism. Cover all target tails and preserve the full state, self exclusion, numerical requirements, and exact masses. Measure against the prescribed objective and validate every candidate with the complete oracle/check suite.

Explore lowering the cost of pair evaluation while retaining the one-target-per-thread mapping as a clear comparison: for example, algebraically cancel target mass in the acceleration expression and evaluate inverse distance with rsqrtf to form an inverse-cube factor. Test arithmetic ordering and only consider FMA or loop unrolling when measurements justify them. These transformations change floating-point rounding: preserve softening and self exclusion, use no global fast-math option, and reject any candidate that fails tolerances, oracle checks, or the nonfinite-output constraint, including extreme-mass and coincident-position cases. Compare on the official geometric-mean metric.
Shared-memory tiling of source particles
tree_details.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json, develop and measure shared-memory source tiling: cooperatively stage source Particle records and reuse each tile across target threads, with correct synchronization and tail handling. Explore tile geometry and legal shared-memory/block settings within the 49,152-byte limit. Preserve the 28-byte Particle layout, entry point, and full input-size correctness; pass all stated edge cases and oracle/tolerance checks. Judge by the official geometric-mean CUDA-event time for N=4096,8192,16384, not by an assumed bandwidth gain.

tree_details.subject: Pairwise force arithmetic and numerical accuracy
tree_details.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, explore an equivalent direct-acceleration formulation that cancels the target mass from the force sum, and selectively evaluate reciprocal-square-root/cube arithmetic or other narrowly scoped math changes. Do not enable global fast math. Preserve softening, update order, exact mass output, and valid behavior for coincident positions, extreme positive masses, and zero or negative dt. Validate all required sizes and oracle tolerances before comparing official benchmark timings; retain slower or inaccurate variants as evidence, not candidates.

tree_details.subject: Register-blocked output mapping and launch geometry
tree_details.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json, explore register-blocked output batching: make the kernel honor the configured items_per_block/grid relationship and evaluate a small number of outputs per thread, reusing each loaded source particle across those outputs where beneficial. Tune legal block and items_per_block settings for the three scored sizes. Keep this tree focused on output mapping/register reuse rather than shared-memory staging or a changed force formula, so its results are complementary to the other missions. Preserve complete output and correctness for all required sizes and edge cases; rank by measured geometric-mean kernel time.

tree_details.subject: Shared-memory source tiling
tree_details.objective: Explore conventional block-local source tiling while keeping one target particle per thread and serial traversal of the source dimension, so the main change is reusing staged source particles across output threads. Tune the tile layout and size, block configuration, and dynamic shared-memory setting within the stated launch limits. Handle arbitrary n and tail tiles without extra kernels, buffers, or host preprocessing. Preserve the entry point, Particle layout, complete outputs and masses; pass every supplied correctness case. Evaluate complete source-and-launch candidates using the official search measurements.

tree_details.subject: Per-thread multi-target coarsening
tree_details.objective: Explore register-level output coarsening: have each thread maintain multiple target particles and reuse each loaded source particle across those targets, without shared-memory source staging as the principal mechanism. Tune coarsening and launch parameters while handling all n and tails safely. Preserve the entry point, Particle layout, update order, complete output and exact masses; pass every supplied correctness case. Compare measured source-and-launch candidates under the official protocol.

tree_details.subject: Source-parallel force reduction
tree_details.objective: Explore a distinct mapping that assigns lanes within a warp (or block) to portions of the source-particle reduction for a target, then combines partial force sums. Focus on parallelizing the reduction dimension rather than output coarsening or block-wide source tiling. Handle arbitrary n, self-interaction exclusion, tail sources and reduction synchronization without races or extra launches/buffers. Preserve the entry point, Particle layout, integration order, and exact masses; validate all supplied cases and compare official measurements.

tree_details.subject: Force arithmetic simplification
tree_details.objective: Explore per-interaction arithmetic reductions such as safe factoring of the target-mass term, reciprocal-square-root use, or other instruction simplifications compatible with NVRTC CUDA 12.6.3 and no global fast-math option. Keep self-interaction exclusion unless an alternative is proven safe, preserve float32 state and exact masses, and reject transformations that fail the FP64-oracle tolerances or produce nonfinite output—including on the isolated extreme-mass case. Keep the entry point and single-kernel interface; measure complete source-and-launch candidates using the official protocol.
